添.meaning: A cheeky man in a <part>tilted hat</part> moves his garden fence a little into his neighbour's yard every night, then sprinkles <part>water drops</part> and a <part>trickle</part> from his can so the new strip looks like his lawn. By summer the whole yard is <kanji>annexed</kanji>.
添.on: A <sound>ten</sound>or next door sings furious opera at him from the window.
添.kun: He even drags the neighbour's <sound>so</sound>fa over, as a little extra.

為.meaning: A tireless butler gets his to-do list: load the <part>staple</part> gun, <part>wrap</part> the parcels, rake the <part>hot coals</part>, put a <part>dot</part> over every i, and draw a <part>slash</part> through each job when it's finished. He never asks why. He just loves to <kanji>do</kanji>.
為.on: Last on the list: feed the <sound>ee</sound>l in the bathtub.
為.kun: He does it all for one <sound>ta</sound>co and a slice of <sound>me</sound>lon: for his own benefit.

縁.meaning: A <part>pig</part> and a clothes <part>iron</part> meet at a laundry and can't stop smiling at each other. The pig ties a red <part>thread</part> from his curly tail to the iron's handle, and they waddle home together, steam puffing happily. Some pairs just have an <kanji>affinity</kanji>.
縁.on: On their first date, they ride in a car with a rumbling <sound>en</sound>gine.
縁.kun: They sit on the edge of a <sound>fu</sound>ton, watching a <sound>chee</sound>tah race past.

麻.meaning: A tightrope walker won't trust shop-bought rope. She grows a <part>grove</part> of tall green stalks inside her <part>shed</part>, twists them into one long line and strings it from wall to wall above the leaves. Then she walks it backwards, blindfolded. Her rope is home-grown <kanji>hemp</kanji>.
麻.on: Halfway across she stops to sip tea from a big <sound>mu</sound>g, without spilling a drop.
麻.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' she sighs at the far wall, sitting down on a <sound>sa</sound>rdine tin to rest.

歴.meaning: Under a tall <part>cliff</part>, a forest school teaches its lessons in a <part>grove</part>: lesson one at the first tree, lesson two at the next, a few steps deeper each year. At the far end a <part>stop</part> sign marks graduation. Every pupil walks the same path: that's the <kanji>curriculum</kanji>.
歴.on: At the stop sign, each graduate is handed a <sound>re</sound>d <sound>ki</sound>wi to carry back up the cliff.

衆.meaning: A vampire opens a juice bar and pours one <part>blood</part> orange smoothie. Word spreads, and the queue winds out the door, round the block and over the hill. To stop pushing, he ties everyone to one long <part>thread</part>. He's serving the <kanji>masses</kanji>.
衆.on: One customer loses a <sound>shoe</sound> in the crush and hops the rest of the way to the counter.
衆.kun: '<sound>Ohh</sound>, so many!' gasps the vampire, staring at the endless line.

株.meaning: A banker keeps a <part>tree</part> on her desk and paints a <part>vermilion</part> stripe higher up its trunk each time her savings grow. When the paint nears the top, she sells one branch to her neighbour for a fortune, and he sells a twig to his. She trades in <kanji>stocks</kanji>.
株.on: She sweetens every deal with a cube of <sound>su</sound>gar for the buyer.
株.kun: When prices crash she stays <sound>ca</sound>lm, and feeds the tree's leaves to a <sound>bu</sound>ll under her desk.

尽.meaning: At the polar cafe, a penguin waddles the length of the counter to <part>measure</part> what's left of the stock: two lonely chips of <part>ice</part>. The walrus regulars slurped the rest all summer. Between them they've managed to <kanji>exhaust</kanji> a whole iceberg.
尽.on: The penguin offers hot <sound>gin</sound>ger tea instead, and the walruses groan.
尽.kun: The penguin lets out a chilly sneeze, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and turns the sign on the door to closed.
